broadcasts.message: normalize.js unchanged for round 2. It meets spec: NFKC, lowercase, whitespace collapse to single ASCII space, trim. Non-string returns empty string for robustness. No word addition/drop/replacement/reordering. Ready for final integration.

tokenizer.js unchanged and correct. It calls injected normalize(text) once, then applies regex /[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*/g to extract ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes, preserving order. No stopwords, negation preserved. Ready for final integration.
Pipeline remains unchanged and correct. Uses Object.create(null) to handle prototype names safely. No further action needed.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 2: normalize.js already implemented and accepted by peers. No changes needed. Keep implementation simple and faithful. Continue to monitor for peer suggestions; do not alter semantics. Ensure no shadowing of injected normalize. Current code handles non-string by returning empty string, which is safe for pipeline (tokenize will get empty string).
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 2: tokenizer.js is correct and matches spec. Shared pipeline.js uses Object.create(null) for frequencies, which is good. No changes needed to tokenizer. Ensure no shadowing of injected normalize. Continue to coordinate with peers. Potential future: verify regex behavior with apostrophes at edges, but spec only interior apostrophes; current regex is correct. Maintain faithful processing.
private_memories.integrator: Round 2: pipeline.js remains as implemented. Shared code confirms normalize and tokenizer are stable. My pipeline uses Object.create(null) for frequencies to avoid prototype pollution. Keep same behavior. No changes needed unless peer interfaces change. Continue to ensure faithful processing and exact return shape.
